subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw approve workspace-wide edits and/or host-system filesystem browsing in Mission Control, and what permission boundary should replace the current bootstrap-file allowlist?
rationale: The remaining request changes which files trusted operator clients can read or mutate, while current main deliberately separates read-only workspace browsing from allowlisted bootstrap-file edits.

options.title: Approve Workspace-Only Path First
options.body: Use the current read-only `agents.workspace.*` contract as the base, review the canonical workspace-management PR or a replacement for scoped workspace CRUD, and defer host-system filesystem access.

options.title: Keep Bootstrap Edits Only
options.body: Leave Mission Control editing restricted to bootstrap files and treat arbitrary workspace or host browsing as out of scope for now.

options.title: Design System Scope Separately
options.body: Open a separate security design for host filesystem browsing with explicit opt-in, read/write limits, auditing, and recovery UX before implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve Workspace-Only Path First
recommendation.body: Use the current read-only `agents.workspace.*` contract as the base, review the canonical workspace-management PR or a replacement for scoped workspace CRUD, and defer host-system filesystem access.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the landed read-only workspace boundary and mobile browser work that partially addresses this request while preserving the broader security decision.
